app.title: Dispersion Equation for Magneto-Rossby and Alfvén Waves
app.summary: A person sets the background physical parameters of a rotating sphere, the range of azimuthal order to cover, and one or more magnetic field strengths, chosen from a preset list or typed as a comma-separated list. The app solves a quadratic dispersion relation at every order for each field strength. It splits the two roots into fast and slow branches and adds the hydrodynamic baseline and the Alfvén frequencies. The person turns curve families on or off and narrows the axis ranges to zoom into one region of the plot. Every curve is drawn on one overlaid frequency-versus-order plot and listed in a tidy table, which they can download as CSV.

task.text: Compute and overlay the mode-frequency curves of a wave dispersion relation across a sweep of field strengths, so the person can see how the branches respond to the parameters and export the curves.

data.text: Curves computed from an analytic model rather than loaded data: for each curve family and field strength, a frequency at each integer azimuthal order, collected into a tidy long-format table.
data.item: one point on a computed dispersion curve: a curve family, a field strength, an azimuthal order and a frequency

stage.text: exploring the parameter space of a theoretical wave model

mechanism.text: Sidebar inputs set the physical parameters, the order range, the list of field strengths, which curve families to show and the axis limits. Every change re-solves the model and redraws one overlaid line plot and the matching data table, which can be downloaded as CSV.

field.text: dispersion relations of magneto-Rossby and Alfvén waves on a rotating sphere, in solar physics

workflow.name: compute model curves over a parameter sweep, overlay them and export them

steps.here: Number inputs for rotation rate in nHz, radius in metres and density in kg/m³, plus a minimum and maximum azimuthal order. The two orders are swapped with a warning if they are given in the wrong order.

steps.step: choose the set of values to sweep
steps.here: A preset menu of magnetic field lists in gauss, or a custom comma-separated list. If the custom list cannot be parsed, it falls back to a default list.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: For each field strength, the field is converted to an Alfvén speed and a dimensionless magnetic parameter. The quadratic is solved at every order, the roots are split into fast and slow branches by which one lies closer to the hydrodynamic baseline, and the results are converted to nHz.

steps.step: choose which curves to show and zoom in
steps.here: Checkboxes show or hide the hydrodynamic Rossby baseline, the fast and slow branches and the Alfvén branch. Range sliders set the order and frequency axis limits.
All curves are overlaid on one frequency-versus-order plot. Colour marks the field strength and line style marks the wave family, with a legend outside the axes.
A table lists every plotted point (curve, B, m, frequency), and a Download CSV button saves it.

distinctive: The two roots of the quadratic are labelled fast and slow by which one lies closer to the zero-field hydrodynamic solution, at each order.
Physical inputs are made dimensionless (field strength to Alfvén speed to a magnetic parameter scaled by rotation and radius), and eigenvalues are converted back to cyclic frequency in nHz.
Only sectoral modes are computed: the poloidal and toroidal indices are both set to the azimuthal order.
Colour encodes the swept parameter and line style encodes the wave family. The Alfvén branch is drawn at both plus and minus but gets only one legend entry.
The exported table holds only the curves currently switched on, so the CSV matches the plot.
